attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, given as his own guess. Not a quotation of anyone else.

semantics.note: The wording is close, but the normalised claim drops 'Here's my own guess' and records the modality as a firm 'will'. Calling it a guess hedges it much like 'I suspect', so it should not be treated as a high-confidence commitment. 'Heavily' and 'potential future profits' are also left undefined.

contract.note: The contract fairly declines to score the claim. It names no threshold for 'heavily', no profit baseline, no period and no accounting basis. Any scored test would add commitments Marcus did not make. The hedge points the same way.

evidence.note: A real News Corp release dated 2024-05-22 announcing a licensing partnership with OpenAI. It gives no payment amounts and says nothing about OpenAI's profits. It is also a company disclosure, so it is context only.

reviews.rationale: Marcus framed this as his own guess, a hedge similar to 'I suspect'. The claim also gives no measure for 'heavily', no profit baseline and no deadline, so no determinate test is possible. The only evidence item shows a licensing deal exists but gives no payout figures or effect on profit. Under policy the claim is not scored.
